subtasks: S1 read-only export of the plan: Plan / PlanStep objects + an exhaustive template registry (WorkflowMode -> node sequence and dependencies), derived from build_graph()'s edges and compared against the registry in BOTH directions. ZERO change to the execution path -- no execution code reads it. Precedent for the checker: tests/unit/graph/test_conditional_edge_wiring.py introspects builder.branches and compares both halves of the edge/router contract. DELIVERED: backend/graph/plan.py (478 lines) + tests/unit/graph/test_plan_registry.py (304 lines / 24 cases); see the S1 section in prd.md. The registry declares entry + the router's per-mode vocabulary + the per-mode excluded hops rather than a hand-written node list, because the graph is mode-blind (reachable_nodes()).

S2 edges come from the plan: build_graph()'s 18 add_conditional_edges are generated from the registry/Plan, edge-for-edge equivalent, pinned by the existing structural gate plus test_routers.py (876 lines). The entry router is the main subject -- it is the only one whose destinations cannot be read statically (routers.py:80 returns a bare str) and the only member of the existing gate's _NON_LITERAL_ROUTERS exemption.

S3 Goal becomes a first-class input: /start's 26-key initial_state literal plus the single `if req.workflow_mode == "brief":` special case become Goal -> compile; the 11 workflow_mode reader sites converge to one or two, and an unknown mode is REFUSED instead of silently reading as 'trend' (8 of the 11 readers default to it today).

S4 workflow.py layering: the 7 giant endpoints (1397 of 2999 lines = 47%) split along api / application / runtime / artifacts / actions. Boundaries first, then move code -- a pure move with no behaviour change; the /status response shape must stay field-for-field identical.

S5 contract and the gate condition: docs/planning.md -- what Goal and Plan are, the evidence required before a plan may be GENERATED rather than selected (the review's 'simple tasks stay deterministic, only complex ones get planned'), and the three things this task explicitly does not do.
notes: P2C PLANNING ROUND (feat/p2c-s1-plan-registry, commit 1ede1941) -- reconnaissance and slice plan, no code yet. The ticket was a blank placeholder (status planning, subtasks [], no prd.md, both jsonl files holding only the example line), so this round produced prd.md with sixteen findings each carrying file:line, a quantified appendix, a rewritten framing, five slices, the red lines, the refusals, the acceptance criteria and three open rulings. THE LOAD-BEARING FINDING: there is no owner of 'the plan'. It exists, but it is DISTRIBUTED -- 18 conditional edges x 18 routers x 11 workflow_mode readers, each re-deriving 'what happens next' from the same state bag, so nothing anywhere can answer 'what is this run going to do'. Quantified: build_graph() (builder.py:69) is a 361-line single function installing 24 nodes, 18 add_conditional_edges and 7 plain edges; routers.py has 27 top-level defs and calls _check_terminal 18 times (:82 through :598); workflow_mode has ELEVEN reader sites, EIGHT of which default to the string 'trend' (routers.py:86/431/467/541/581/605, agents/orchestrator.py:35, agents/copywriter.py:169/389, api/routes/workflow.py:968, db/workflows.py:376). The entry router (routers.py:80) is the one router whose destinations cannot be read -- it returns a bare str and is the sole member of test_conditional_edge_wiring.py:31's _NON_LITERAL_ROUTERS exemption -- and inside it the phase -> node table is written TWICE, once per mode (:90-101 brief, :104-113 trend), ending in a silent fallback (:116) that routes an unknown phase to that mode's start node. The same decision is therefore made twice: OrchestratorAgent.execute (agents/orchestrator.py:19-40, the whole file is 40 lines) compresses state into a phase by pure deterministic if-chain, and orchestrator_router expands it back into a node. SO THE TICKET'S PREMISE IS REWRITTEN: what is missing is not a Planner, it is 'the plan' as a statable object -- step one of dynamic planning is making today's implicit plan exportable, not generating a new one, and the testable criterion follows from that (given a checkpoint, can you say which nodes remain without executing the graph? today: no, you would have to simulate 18 routers). Likewise 'stop adding workflow_mode + router + edge' must become a MECHANISM (a mode missing from the registry turns a test red, following the exhaustive-registry precedent of RETRY_POLICIES / TAKEOVER_HAZARDS), not a convention. Vocabulary facts that shape the design: WorkflowMode already exists at state/enums.py:60 with exactly two members and a docstring saying 'determines starting node and pipeline path' (so the template need not be invented, only declared as data); ExecutionMode (state/enums.py:53, single/continuous) is an orthogonal axis this task must not touch; WorkflowPhase (state/enums.py:6) has 13 members of which ENGAGING is legacy (every router maps it to __end__ at :97/:110) and PLANNING means 'go to content_strategist' (:92/:106) -- so the word collides with what this task means by a plan; and TaskType (config/models.py:6) is a MODEL ROUTING KEY, so the Task object from the review's six core objects (not yet built: ArtifactRef is P1a state/artifacts.py:85, RunContext is P1b context/models.py:121, ToolResult is P1c tools/runtime/models.py:281, ActionIntent / DecisionRecord are P2a creator_agent/models.py:669/:503) must be named around it. Goal is not an object today either: 12 _run_graph_and_persist call sites across 5 files (workflow.py 7, review.py:204/:385, optimization.py:93/:157, blogger.py:118) each hand-build an initial state, and /start's is a 26-key literal (workflow.py:712-740) whose only mode difference is one `if req.workflow_mode == "brief":` at :742 gating whether the brief body goes to the Artifact Store or stays inline (:744-760). workflow.py itself is now 2999 lines (the ticket says 2519 -- it grew 480) with 49 top-level defs, the top seven holding 1397 lines (resume_workflow 327 at :1288, get_workflow_status 244 at :874, start_workflow 193 at :678, retry_publish 179 at :2821, recover_workflow 159 at :1618, retry_ripple_analysis 153 at :2159, stream_workflow_progress 142 at :1835), and each of those seven touches between two and six of seven probed concerns (DB write / events / state construction / graph execution / response body / artifacts / leases) -- start_workflow and retry_publish touch six. What makes the slices affordable: the topology ALREADY has a structural gate (test_conditional_edge_wiring.py compares a router's Literal return set against its path map at :78 and every path-map target against the real node set at :115, and its docstring records the P1d KeyError: '__end__' incident), and the graph test surface is 1581 lines across 7 files while 28 test files touch build_graph / workflow_mode / add_conditional_edges -- so an equivalence-preserving rewrite has strong tripwires, provided the reshape-do-not-delete discipline is followed point by point. BASELINE measured this round: ruff check clean, ruff format --check 520 files, mypy backend --python-version 3.12 207 files, pytest 3414 passed / 3 skipped. HONEST SCOPE NOTES: the two WorkflowPhase definitions (state/enums.py:6 as StrEnum and api/generated/models.py:49 as Enum) are member-identical 13/13 today, so this is a DUPLICATE, not a DRIFT -- registered as a latent drift surface and deliberately not merged, because nothing behaves differently and api/generated/** is a generated artifact; the plan's 31 cited anchors were verified line by line against the tree this round, and one (agents/orchestrator.py) was corrected from 22-42 to 19-40 in the process. The three open rulings are recorded in the prd: the granularity of PlanStep (node vs P1c capability -- node first, because it is exportable with zero risk, capability deferred to S3), the behaviour for an unknown Goal/mode (refuse with a named error, which is a real behaviour change needing a ruling), and whether S5 stays a document or becomes the dynamic path itself if S1-S4 produce evidence for it (follow the evidence, not the plan). status and completedAt deliberately left untouched, as is this repo's convention. P2C S1 ROUND (feat/p2c-s1-plan-registry) -- delivered backend/graph/plan.py (478 lines) + tests/unit/graph/test_plan_registry.py (304 lines / 24 cases); execution path untouched (build_graph() unchanged, no production module imports it). THE SHAPE CHANGED FROM THE TICKET'S WORDING, deliberately and on measured grounds: the ticket asked for 'WorkflowMode -> node sequence and dependencies', i.e. a hand-written per-mode node list; the graph is MODE-BLIND (24 of 24 nodes reachable from orchestrator, and the SAME 22 from either mode's entry -- reachable_nodes()), so mode membership cannot be derived from topology, and a hand-written node list would be a declaration nothing could corroborate. The registry therefore declares only entry + the router's full per-mode vocabulary + the per-mode EXCLUDED HOPS, each naming the router that decides it, and the node set is EXPORTED from build_graph(). Small enough that every part is corroborated: the five mode-conditional routers already have behaviour tests, and the entry is now corroborated by CALLING orchestrator_router -- which also closes a real gap, since its brief branch had no test at all (brief_analyzer appeared in tests only via the three ripple routers and node-level tests). THE DEFECT FOUND AND REGISTERED, NOT FIXED: orchestrator_router answers 'copywriter' for brief mode at phase=creating (routers.py:93) while builder.py:168-174's orchestrator path map has no such key; CREATING is not terminal, so the branch is reachable, and reaching it is the P1d failure mode again (a router answer with no map entry -> KeyError inside langgraph, on a path no test watches). Latent only because nothing observed reaches orchestrator with phase=creating. Fixing it means adding a map key = a behaviour change, and S1's contract is zero change, so it lives in UNRESOLVED_ROUTER_VALUES with a REVERSE assertion: once the map is fixed the exemption goes stale, plan_registry_complaints() reports exemption_no_longer_applies, and test_state_graph_and_registry_agree goes red -- so the exemption has to be deleted explicitly instead of rotting. SECOND MEASURED ASYMMETRY: Branch.ends is the path map itself ({router answer: node}), so reading it as a sequence yields ANSWERS, not DESTINATIONS; exactly one row across the 18 branches differs -- evaluator_gate's 'publisher' -> publish_gate (builder.py:394). The existing wiring test reads the keys and is CORRECT for what it checks (a router's answer must be a key), but the destination side was never checked; a keys-based export looks right on 17 of 18 branches and on the eighteenth publishes an edge the graph cannot take (evaluator_gate -> publisher, bypassing the human authorisation gate) and drops publish_gate from the plan entirely. GATES: ruff 522 files clean, ruff format --check 522, mypy 208 files clean, baseline drift within threshold, tool runtime gate OK, pytest 3438 passed 3 skipped (baseline 3414 + 24 new cases). MUTATION SELF-CHECK: 22/22 killed, 0 survived, restore=OK, plus M14 registered as an equivalent mutation (trend's plan is a strict subset of brief's, so |= and last-wins agree). Two triage findings: M11 survived twice and turned out to target DEAD CODE -- it removed followed_by's 'dst in node_set' filter, a condition that is never false because the plan is the set reachable from the root through kept edges; the condition was DELETED rather than covered, while preceded_by keeps its filter (M10 shows it is load-bearing, since a predecessor can sit outside the plan). M14 is equivalent and is labelled as such rather than papered over with a contrived test.
